**Scope stance (offline/hermetic + CC9 matched-budget-or-refuse).** Everything below is the
**winning candidate** (E1 kernel; E5a crossing mechanism), measured offline. Non-winning
candidates (E2/E3 kernels; the E5b/E5c splits), the official-SDK MCP/ACP calls, cross-*candidate*
hash-chain identity, and the two-toolchain CI / cross-ecosystem serialization multiplier all need
foreign toolchains, network SDK fetches, or a second-ecosystem reviewer — **not runnable
hermetically and not matchable-budget offline (CC9)**. They are **deferred with compensating
controls, never fabricated** (DF-S0.3-1/-2/-3). The revalidation rule (ADR-0050 §6 trigger 5)
turns on the winning candidate, which **is** measured; the ADR-0050 §4 kernel-family robustness
(E1-kernel wins 0.979 of corners; survives every adversarial sweep) is why the non-winning
candidates are not decision-load-bearing.

## S1 — kernel slice: correctness gates G1–G4

Executable deterministic unit tests in `spikes/s1-kernel-spike/src/lib.rs` (run by the runner via
`cargo test`). **All pass.**

| gate | verifies | result | test |
|---|---|---|---|
| **G1** | hash chain deterministic for the shared corpus (canonical form implementation-independent) + pinned 64-hex known-answer | **pass** | `g1_hash_chain_is_deterministic` |
| **G2** | rebuild-equality: `project()` from scratch == incremental at every `until_seq` | **pass** | `g2_rebuild_equals_incremental` |
| **G3** | crash mid-append: no partial multi-event append visible on replay; stale writer fenced by `lease_generation` | **pass** | `g3_crash_no_partial_append`, `g3_stale_writer_fenced` |
| **G4** | 64 KiB event offloaded + blob resolvable; > 2^53 integer round-trips | **pass** | `g4_offload_and_numeric_round_trip` |

> G1 note: the *cross-candidate* byte-identity (E2/E3 produce the same chain) needs the other
> ecosystems — **deferred DF-S0.3-1**; the within-candidate determinism + known-answer is proven
> here. G4 note: arbitrary-precision *decimal-string* numerals are the `idp/1` form deferred to
> S1.2 (DF-S0.1-2 interim); the Stage-0 canonical form carries i64, which covers > 2^53 exactly.

## S1 — measurements M-S1-1…9 (N = 5: median · min–max)

| id | metric | unit | median | min–max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **M-S1-1** | process start → first ledger event visible | ms | **10.6** | 9.77 – 11.8 |
| **M-S1-2** | resident memory per idle session at N=50 (RSS/50) | MiB | **3.74** | 3.38 – 3.93 |
| **M-S1-3** | sustained durable append throughput at N=50 (aggregate) | events/s | **3 791** | 3 475 – 4 160 |
| **M-S1-4** | `project()` rebuild (200 events) | ms | **~0.0001** | 0 – 0.0001 |
| **M-S1-4** | `project()` incremental update per event | µs | **0.137** | 0.134 – 0.286 |
| **M-S1-5** | fan-out ratio N=50/N=1 — **CPU/concurrency** (core-normalized) | ratio | **1.58** | 1.25 – 1.71 |
| **M-S1-5** | fan-out ratio N=50/N=1 — CPU (raw wall) | ratio | 6.59 | 5.20 – 7.12 |
| **M-S1-5** | fan-out ratio N=50/N=1 — **durable** (fsync-bound, see note) | ratio | 20.1 | 18.1 – 22.2 |
| **M-S1-5** | achieved parallelism at N=50 (effective concurrent sessions) | — | 47.8 | 47.7 – 48.0 |
| **M-S1-6** | sandboxed call overhead: **helper-binary** round-trip − bare command | ms | **0.08** | 0.041 – 0.274 |
| **M-S1-7** | MCP call round-trip; ACP session setup | ms | **n/a{offline_no_official_sdk}** (DF-S0.3-1) | — |
| **M-S1-8** | cancellation latency: cancel → all N=50 tasks stopped | ms | **4.25** | 3.27 – 7.47 |
| **M-S1-9** | streaming tail lag at N=50 — **median** | µs | **5** | 4 – 6 |
| **M-S1-9** | streaming tail lag at N=50 — **p95** | µs | **23** | 16 – 64 |

**M-S1-5 caveat (host + storage, R3).** On a 12-core host, N=50 cannot run truly parallel, so a
raw wall ratio is core-bound; the **durable** ratio (~20×) is additionally **fsync-serialization
bound** — the durable-before-visible path fsyncs per batch on per-session WALs with no group
commit (a pessimistic throwaway design), so at N=50 the disk serializes commits. Neither is the
*ecosystem concurrency mechanism* C5 scores. The l1-spike-spec frames fan-out as "ideal 1.0 if
perfectly parallel on ≥50 cores" (CPU-parallel), so the C5 input is the **CPU/concurrency
core-normalized** ratio (1.58) — corroborated by achieved parallelism 47.8/50 (the mechanism does
run all 50 sessions concurrently), cancel 4.25 ms, and tail p95 23 µs. The durable ratio is
reported for completeness with this caveat.

## S2 — boundary slice: measurements M-S2-1…7 (N = 5: median · min–max)

Winning split **E5a** crossing mechanism, measured **matched E1↔E1** (both arms E1 — CC9) to
isolate the transport cost. Binding (b): subprocess over stdio, newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0.

| id | metric | unit | median | min–max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **M-S2-1** | per-run crossing overhead (split − native, N=50, 4 crossings/run) | µs/run | **73** | 70 – 146 |
| **M-S2-1** | per-run crossing overhead as % of a representative run wall (M-S1-5 N=1 ≈ 130 ms) | % | **≈ 0.056 %** | — |
| **M-S2-2** | per-sample crossing overhead (the *disallowed* hot path) — median | µs | **21** | 20 – 55 |
| **M-S2-2** | per-sample crossing overhead — p95 | µs | 31 | 26 – 92 |
| **M-S2-3** | serialize + hash-verify per event on the far side — 16 KiB | µs | **141** | 130 – 148 |
| **M-S2-3** | serialize + hash-verify per event on the far side — 64 KiB | µs | **526** | 501 – 554 |
| **M-S2-4** | codegen round-trip (export → codegen → drift-checked bindings) | ms | **26** | 26 – 201 |
| **M-S2-5** | two-toolchain CI (clean build + test of both sides) | min | **n/a{offline_single_toolchain}** (DF-S0.3-2) | — |
| **M-S2-6** | `hello` version-mismatch refusal **and** resume after killed peer | pass/fail | **PASS** | pass (all 5) |
| **M-S2-7** | hash-equality of every far-side event (100 % required) | % | **100** | 100 (all 5) |

**M-S2-6 detail:** version-mismatch refusal → typed `ContractMajorUnsupported` (closed error sum,
ADR-0178 D2), never a silent fallback — **pass**; resume-after-killed-peer → a fresh peer
re-handshakes after the peer is killed (the Stage-0 form; full `open_session(resume)` session
state lands at Stage 1) — **pass**.

**DF-S0.1-1 durable-frame / ephemeral columns (now discharged):** durable-frame delivery latency
p50 = **5 µs**, p95 = **23 µs** (= the M-S1-9 subscribe tail lag over the durable-before-visible
stream at N=50 fan-out); **ephemeral-drop rate = 0** (every appended frame is delivered; the
subscribe channel drops none). Per-crossing / per-run connection bounds (M-S2-1/-2) are the
`hh-embed/1 §2.4` connection-bounds MUST-data (OQ-402), recorded here and carried to S1.25.

## Revalidation determination (ADR-0050 §6 trigger 5 → feeds GATE-G1)

- **Winning-candidate gates:** G1–G4 **pass**, M-S2-6 **pass**, M-S2-7 **100 %** → **no gate-failure trigger**.
- **C5:** measured 4 vs assumed 5 → |Δ| = 1 → **within band**.
- **C7:** measured 4 (strict) / 5 (per §5 non-discrimination note) vs assumed 5 → |Δ| ≤ 1 → **within band**.
- **C12:** the measured transport/codegen/hash-equality components are **favorable and do not
  contradict** the assumed E5a value of 2; the polyglot-specific conjunct that the assumed 2 is
  *about* (two resident runtimes' CI + cross-ecosystem serialization) is **deferred (DF-S0.3-2)**
  and re-scored at Stage 3 (kernel↔lab boundary first exercised with the E2 lab). No score is
  fabricated from a transport-only measurement, so **no C12 trigger is asserted**.

**Verdict: the ADR-0009 / ADR-0050 ecosystem decision HOLDS. No revalidation trigger fires.** The
`unmeasured-by-spike` (`u`) marks on **C5** and **C7** for the E1 kernel may be cleared in the
ADR-0050 amendment log (measured 4/4, within the assumed ±1 band). The **C12 `u` mark stays** — its
polyglot conjunct is deferred to Stage 3. GATE-G1 (the phase-synthesis agent) evaluates whether
the deferred cross-candidate / polyglot measurements (DF-S0.3-1/-2/-3) require an online spike
budget before Stage 1; the kernel-family robustness (ADR-0050 §4) is the compensating control.
